snp3.7:0.2: This sutta is identical with MN 92; part of it also appears at Mv VI.35.1–8.
snp3.7:2.2: According to Mv VI.35.3, at this point in the story Keṇiya offered a juice drink to the Buddha, who told him to offer it to the Saṅgha as well; this became the occasion for the allowance permitting monks to drink juice drinks after noon.
snp3.7:17.2: To be a wheel-turner meant, in ancient Indian parlance, to rule the entire “wheel” of the eight directions; SN 56:11, in saying the Buddha’s first sermon set the Dhamma-wheel rolling, borrows this image to show that his Dhamma rules in every direction. The Dhamma-wheel is also a “wheel” in the sense of a list of permutations: the first sermon’s Dhamma-wheel lists all twelve permutations of the four noble truths crossed with the three levels of knowledge appropriate to each—knowledge of the truth, of the task it entails, and that the task has been done.
snp3.7:17.4: An epithet for the Indian subcontinent.
snp3.7:22.5: See MN 141. Some translations of this verse mistakenly have Sāriputta keep the Dhamma-wheel rolling as the Buddha’s successor rather than as the disciple right below him; this has led at least one scholar to treat the verse as a late addition, in seeming conflict with MN 108 (which says the Buddha left no successor) and SN 47:13 (which notes that Sāriputta predeceased the Buddha). Correctly translated, though, there is no conflict.
snp3.7:23.4: Three of the four duties with regard to the four noble truths. See SN 56:11 and MN 149.
snp3.7:28.3: Sela, despite his newfound confidence in the Buddha, has not yet abandoned his racism; AN 4:85 has the Buddha redefine the brahmanical idea of dark birth in terms of kamma rather than race.
snp3.7:35.2: Chandas normally means “meter,” but can also mean Vedic hymn; see the discussion in The Buddhist Monastic Code, volume II, chapter 8. On the Sāvitti as the chief Vedic hymn, see Sn 3:4, note 4.
